title: Rav Natan bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Chullin 45b: he sat before Rav and examined whether the greater part of the spinal membrane and the greater part of the cord tissue were intact. Rav told him, “If most of its membrane is intact, this cord tissue makes no difference,” etc. Hyman states that the name should actually read Rav Natan bar Abba, as cited in Dikdukei Soferim, note 3 there.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The heading remains Natan bar Avin. Hyman proposes Natan bar Abba for the Chullin 45b passage, citing דק״ס (conventionally Dikdukei Soferim), note/letter 3. His proposed correction does not replace the heading or settle an identity.

The discussion concerns the spinal membrane and cord tissue. לא מעלה in this abbreviated quotation means that the tissue’s condition makes no difference when most of the membrane remains intact; it does not mean that the tissue independently makes the animal fit.
